name: English
title: HSCL1 - one system, three modes
description: HSCL1 is an experimental Linux workstation based on Kubuntu 26.04: a Workstation desktop, an isolated Security Lab and a privacy workflow. Pre-release, tested in virtual machines only.

hero.sub: HSCL1 is a Kubuntu-based Linux workstation with its own desktop look, a command-line tool and an installer. It is an early pre-release that has been tested in virtual machines only.

modes.d: The everyday desktop: HCS Hybrid Desktop on KDE Plasma with a top bar, a floating dock, a Control Center and the hscl command-line tool.
Planned: Kali tools in rootless containers or virtual machines, never from the host's package sources. Not implemented yet.
Planned: a Tor workflow and a launcher for the official Tails image. No anonymity claim is made, and none will be made without tests.

honest_h: What is verified, and what is not
honest: Boots to a live desktop and installs to a virtual disk in QEMU (UEFI and BIOS). Tested only in virtual machines.
Not tested on physical hardware. Not signed. Secure Boot inside the guest has not been read yet.
Security Lab and Privacy are planned, not shipped.

HSCL1 is not an official Kubuntu, Kali or Tails product and is not endorsed by them. HSCL1 is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Tails project. KALI LINUX™ is a trademark of OffSec. Third-party names belong to their owners.

dl.none: Release not published yet. See the source repository for build instructions.
dl.parts_note: GitHub limits a release file to 2 GiB, so the ISO is split into parts of about 1.5 GB. Download all parts and SHA256SUMS, then join and verify them.
verify: Download every .part file and SHA256SUMS into one folder (for example with: gh release download TAG -R timfromhcs/HSCL1).
Run scripts/release-join.sh from the source repository. It checks every part and the final image against SHA256SUMS and refuses to continue on a mismatch.
Compare the SHA-256 of the joined ISO with the value on this page.
limits: Virtual machines only; no physical hardware has been tested.
This image still has KDE Connect listening on port 1716; the fix is in the source but not in this image.

sec.title: Security and limits - HSCL1
sec.intro: HSCL1 is early pre-alpha software. Do not use it for anything that needs a security guarantee. This page says what we do and what we do not claim.
sec.report: Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on the source repository (Security tab, Report a vulnerability). Please do not open a public issue for a security problem. Include the version (hscl version), what you did, what happened and what you expected. There is no service-level promise at this stage.
integrity: Releases are published with SHA256SUMS; verify every download against it.
Release signing is not in place yet. No signing key has been created, so treat releases as unsigned.
claims: No anonymity: HSCL1 is not Tails, and the Privacy mode is planned, not shipped.
No guarantee against attacks, no certification, no claim that it is hard to hack.
No support for physical hardware: no device has been tested.
Secure Boot: the image boots under Secure Boot firmware in a virtual machine, but the Secure Boot state inside the guest has not been read, so no Secure Boot claim is made.
sec.dev: The Workshop is a developer tool that is inactive by default: no enabled service, no socket and no network listener. It starts only when a hypervisor provides a dedicated virtual port, or when an administrator starts it by hand. Whoever controls that port already controls the virtual machine, and its hooks run as root by design. Do not enable it on a machine you do not control.
sec.docs: The full, maintained lists are in the source repository.

vm.title: Try HSCL1 in a virtual machine - HSCL1
vm.h1: Try HSCL1 in a virtual machine
vm.intro: The only way HSCL1 has been tested so far is in virtual machines. These are the exact settings of our automated tests. Do not write this early pre-release to a USB stick for a real computer: it has not been tested on physical hardware.
rows: QEMU 11.1 on Windows with WHPX acceleration; software emulation (TCG) where acceleration was unavailable (the Secure Boot firmware test)
UEFI (OVMF/edk2) and legacy BIOS (SeaBIOS) both reached the live desktop
Standard VGA (software rendering); HSCL1 detects this and turns animations and blur off
One empty 40 GB virtio disk in qcow2 format, created only for the test
QEMU user-mode networking with a virtio network card
The ISO attached as a read-only CD-ROM
steps: The live desktop appears after roughly two minutes with hardware acceleration; with software emulation it takes much longer.
The installer (Calamares) asks you to choose the disk. Nothing is preselected and nothing is written until you confirm the summary. Use a disposable virtual disk.
A full test installation took about 23 minutes in our run and booted from the virtual disk afterwards.
not: VirtualBox, VMware and Hyper-V: no settings are recommended because none were tested.
KVM on Linux: the same QEMU options should work, but this has not been verified by us.
3D acceleration, USB passthrough and shared folders: not tested; keep shared folders off.
vm.script: The harness that runs these tests is scripts/qemu_boot_test.py in the source repository.
